content:
#15 Created an account I can comment on this.

The cloudflare solution poses several practical problems for me. First of all, I use a browser setup that does not store cookies across sessions, causing the verification to pop up each new session.

That would in and of itself would not be much of an issue. However, the loading time of this verification on my phone is around 30 seconds long. This makes the visiting the website prohibitively slow for me.

Further, because of joint issues I depend on voice control of my computer. In my browser I use a plugin that annotates every clickable element with a short character sequence I can utter to click it. However, the verification button of cloudflare is not recognized as a clickable element. I can only assume that this is meant to trick bots, but in practice this forces me to use the physical mouse to prove that I am human.

Many other websites I frequent have started using anubis [1] to limit the impact from AI scraping. It serves the same end as the cloudflare solution, but does not require user interaction and has been fast enough to not cause any issues on my mobile device. It works by challenging the client with a cryptographic puzzle, small enough to not be a nuisance for humans to wait for their computer to solve but large enough to make it economically unviable to scrape en masse. Perhaps this could also be a solution for the nlab, a site I cherish dearly.

[1] https://github.com/TecharoHQ/anubis

content:
#16 Hi Erik, we considered anubis but I felt like it would require more maintenance than the cloudflare solution and I am not sure if the approach they take to defend bots is sound in general (e.g. see https://lock.cmpxchg8b.com/anubis.html). Outsourcing that to cloudflare means they would have deal with how to fight against bots and could upgrade their approach however is effective.

Anyway, because the wiki mostly caches all pages we only deployed cloudflare for the wiki because of the anonymous file locking problem. We are considering other ways to address the problem of anonymous file locking and would prefer to use neither of anubis or cloudflare.

@Mike: Unfortunately we can only configure the lifetime of cookies (currently 7 days). It seems like they also store the client’s ip address in the cookie somehow, invalidating the cookie in case you change the network. I am investigating if we can soften that somewhat, but I fear this is not possible or we would need to upgrade to an enterprise plan.

content:
#22 Due to issues that people are reporting (here and in another thread) the Cloudflare protection for the nLab has been removed again (for the nForum it remains in place, I think).

We can maybe deal with the bots on the nLab in another way: Since the nLab is good at caching, the only problem the bots cause here is in inadvertently “locking” entries, which results in those frequent spurious warning messages you get to see: “Anonymous has been editing this entry for X minutes.” So I guess we could just make “Anonymous” not be able to lock entries (which would make all the more sense since “Anonymous” is already forbidden from submitting entries).
